name: Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-26. A finetune of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, not a new base model: same config.json, same 27.781 params (identical tensor set), so the whole model fits exactly where models/qwen3-8-27b fits - hybrid Gated DeltaNet with 16 full-attention layers of 64, KV 65,536 B/token is unchanged, active params equal total. HARDWARE GATE: passes (27.781 <= 40 active, 13.9 GiB at 0.5 GiB/params <= 128) and it is the *best* shape in its class for this box - the linear-attention layers mean the KV cache is a quarter of a dense 27B's, and the point of the model is the opposite direction from more compute.

WHY IT IS WORTH A RECORD, and the honest headline: it is NOT a capability upset. The card's own table shows Swift 1.5 ahead on 4 rows (LiveCodeBench v6 81.71 vs 76.76, Terminal-Bench 2.1 72.13 vs 69.21, C-Eval 90.92 vs 90.00, GPQA-Diamond 88.59 vs 88.28) and BEHIND on 4 (IFBench 72.07 vs 73.53, ERQA 65.40 vs 67.45, AIME 2026 96.00 vs 98.67, HMMT Nov 2025 97.33 vs 99.33). Two of the four wins are +0.31 and +0.92, i.e. inside five-seed noise, and the real claim is the one the card leads with: 58.5% fewer thinking tokens at roughly parity on accuracy, which is a throughput story, not a quality story. It earns the record because a same-harness bf16 base column is printed for every row - rare, and it is what makes the regressions legible: rejecting overthinking costs hard-math headroom (AIME -2.67, HMMT -2.00) and instruction-following (IFBench -1.46).

BASE-COLUMN DISCIPLINE: the 'Qwen3.8' column is the vendor's own re-run of the base under the printed protocol (BF16, vLLM 0.27.1, Qwen3 parser, context 262,144, thinking xhigh, temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20, mean of five seeds 0-4; Terminal-Bench at context 131,072 on the same Harbor build, five trials per task), not a copied figure from Qwen's card. That is why its base numbers differ from the base record's own rows - e.g. GPQA 88.28 here vs 89.2 ingested from Qwen's card, Terminal-Bench 69.21 vs 73.0. Do not average the two columns together; the base record's rows describe Qwen's published run and these describe UkisAI's.

LICENCE: gated, swift-open-license-1.0, a bespoke non-OSI licence with an enterprise tier. The weights are downloadable after accepting the gate; commercial terms are not Apache-2.0 like the base.

PEDIGREE CAVEAT: Swift 1.5 was trained FROM Swift 1.0 (ukisai's earlier Qwen3.8-27B derivative, ~350k downloads), not from the base checkpoint directly, so the delta above is Swift-1.0-plus-more-RL versus stock Qwen3.8-27B, and this repo does not isolate the two stages.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v6
benchmarks.config: Card HTML table, column 'Swift 1.5'; base column 'Qwen3.8' 76.76 in the same table (+4.95). Both arms re-run by the vendor under one printed harness: BF16, vLLM 0.27.1, Qwen3 parser, context 262,144, thinking xhigh, temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20, average over five seeds 0-4. Base column is a real bf16 run of Qwen3.8-27B on that harness, not a copied card figure.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.config: Same card table, Swift 1.5 vs base Qwen3.8 69.21 (+2.92). Both served at context 131,072 on the same Harbor build, five trials per task. Card footnote flags the token-saving figure as misleading on this row, not the accuracy figure. LOSS relative to the base record's own vendor row for Terminal Bench 2.1 (73.0, Terminus harness, [INGESTED 2026-10-23]) - the two rows are not the same run.

benchmarks.name: C-Eval
benchmarks.config: Same card table, Swift 1.5 vs base Qwen3.8 90.00 (+0.92) over five seeds. Output cap 16,384 as printed in the methodology table.

benchmarks.name: GPQA-Diamond
benchmarks.config: Same card table, Swift 1.5 vs base Qwen3.8 88.28 (+0.31) over five seeds, thinking xhigh. The margin is far inside seed noise, so this is a tie, not a win. The base catalog record carries 89.2 for GPQA Diamond from Qwen's own card - a different run, so the two must not be blended.

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.config: Same card table. LOSS: base Qwen3.8 73.53 beats Swift 1.5 72.07 by 1.46, recorded deliberately - the token-efficiency post-train costs instruction-following on the strict metric.

benchmarks.name: ERQA
benchmarks.config: Same card table. LOSS: base Qwen3.8 67.45 beats Swift 1.5 65.40 by 2.05.

benchmarks.name: AIME 2026
benchmarks.config: Same card table. LOSS: base Qwen3.8 98.67 beats Swift 1.5 96.00 by 2.67 over five seeds - rejecting overthinking loops loses hard-math headroom.

benchmarks.config: Same card table. LOSS: base Qwen3.8 99.33 beats Swift 1.5 97.33 by 2.00.
